text:
phil: Heads up — canary publish for redwood/service-login:staging-20260320-abc123 failed in eu-west-1.
phil: Deploy bot rejected the manifest due to provenance attestation: layer compression mismatch.
deploy-bot: publish rejected — provenance_guard: attestation failure: layer 3 compression 'zstd' != recorded 'gzip' (manifest digest: sha256:deadbeef...)
maya: Ugh. We switched the build worker to zstd to save size last week, didn't update the attest pipeline.
maya: This is why we have prov checks. Can we re-run with gzip or update attestation metadata?
ci-bot: build job #4821: reproduced locally. `docker save` shows layer 3 compressed with zstd. Previous successful publish (sha256:c0ffee...) used gzip.
olivia: Quick question — did the image get promoted anywhere or is it only stuck in staging registry? I want to know rollback impact.
phil: Only staging canary. No promotion. But deploybot skipped the canary step, so user-facing rollout didn't happen.
sam: Proposal: pin service-login in the canary route to previous digest (sha256:c0ffee...) and block new rollouts until we rebuild with gzip.
maya: Agreed. I'll trigger a rebuild on the gzip runner and attach a new attestation. ETA ~30m.
phil: For now let's pin and open a rollback ticket. @release-manager — please hold release notes update for login feature until we confirm.
olivia: Will do. I'll add a note in the release doc and mark change window as delayed 1h.
deploy-bot: action: route pin applied to canary -> sha256:c0ffee... (applied by phil).
sam: Also let's add a lint check in the build pipeline to ensure compression algorithm is explicit and recorded in provenance metadata.
maya: I'll add that to the build PR and include a migration script to recompress layers if needed.
ci-bot: FYI debugging snippet: ```
$ skopeo inspect docker://eu-west-1.registry.redwood/service-login:staging-20260320-abc123
"Layers": [
  "sha256:aaa... (gzip)",
  "sha256:bbb... (gzip)",
  "sha256:deadbeef... (zstd)"
]
```
phil: Thanks — once maya posts the rebuilt image and prov attestation, deploybot can re-run canary. Keep me posted.
maya: Will comment here when pushed and attested. :hourglass:
olivia: Tracking note: release-notes PR #512 will be updated after canary verification.
phil: TL;DR: canary blocked by compression mismatch, temporary pin to previous digest, rebuild w/ gzip required, follow-up: pipeline lint for compression, release note hold.
